title: Runlog setup (schema version 1)
description: What a tool attached to the game is set to while a run lasts, and what the player is handed to start with. Written for a tool rather than for a pack, so one fits every pack for the same game.

kind.description: What this document is. A pack says `pack`; this says `setup`.

schemaVersion.description: The format's major version, as a pack carries one.

id.description: Reverse-domain id, the way a pack is identified: `com.example.setups.bare-handed`.

version.description: Semantic version. A setup that changes what it does changes this, or nobody holding it is offered the new one.

title.description: What it is called, on a card and in a chooser.

author.description: Who wrote it, for a card and a list. A setup travels on its own, so this is the only credit it carries.

description.description: What playing under it is like, in a line or two.

tool.description: The tool this is for, by the name that tool calls itself when it attaches.

op.description: The operation, in the tool's own vocabulary: `flag.set`, `runes.give`. A tool refuses by name anything its build does not have.

args.description: What the operation takes. Its shape is the tool's business, not this format's.

once.description: Given one time in a run rather than every time a tool attaches. The terms go out on every attach, because a tool that restarted is holding none of them and a setting applied twice is the same setting. A gift is not: runes handed over on every reconnect is a different game by the third one.

ops.description: What to do when a tool attaches, in order.

license.description: As a pack carries one. Absent means the author said nothing, which is not the same as permission.

id.description: An SPDX identifier where there is one, else whatever name the terms go by.

redistributable.description: Whether somebody may pass this on. False means it was shared with you, not given to you.
